title: Protection
text: “We were just trying to return that child to where she belongs…”

That’s the kind of excuse the adventurers are making. “Where she belongs” is such an abstract way of putting it, isn’t it? Does that mean back with the slave trader? After all, since she was here from the very beginning, isn’t this den where she belongs?

Meanwhile, a plump monster with dragon-like features is currently snarling menacingly, and the Assistant is clinging to it as if to protect it. She’s looking back and forth between Keel and Father with a stunned expression.
“Judging by that conversation just now, I really can’t believe that… I’m sorry, but as for that child…”
My father scanned the interior of the lair. The only living monster inside was the one the Assistant was already clinging to.
“The eggs…”
At my father’s words, the adventurers scooped up the remaining eggs as if to say, “These are our treasure.” My father let out a deep sigh.
“Then, I’ll take custody of the monster that’s with that child.”
“B-but—”
Just as the adventurers’ representative was about to object, my father glared at him—even though his face was hidden by his hood.
“It doesn’t matter who takes it in, does it? Or were you guys planning to do something other than ‘take it in’ when I wasn’t looking?”
“Uh… o-okay. But since it’s a Demi-Human with a monster, I think it might be dangerous.”
Ignoring the adventurer’s words, my father walked over to his Assistant.
“Gauuuuuu…”
The monster clinging to the Assistant groaned as Father approached.
“It’s okay, I won’t do anything.”

The monster looked dumbfounded as Father gently reached out his hand. I know this, you see. I know that Father is someone monsters take a liking to. Of course, monsters are monsters, and as long as he doesn’t use his Monster Mark, I can’t completely rule out the possibility that it might attack. Was he saying this to the Assistant?
“For now… you—all of you—should get out of here. Otherwise, you might end up in even worse trouble. So please, come with us.”
“That’s right! There are a lot of nasty guys around here, so if you don’t run, you’ll be in big trouble!”
Father and Keel reached out to the Assistant, but she refused to move, still clinging to the monster.
“No…”
“But… if things stay like this, you’ll…”
“I’m waiting for my dad to come back… otherwise, he’ll be sad when he gets home.”

Who exactly is this “dad” the assistant is talking about? Considering the context of the conversation and the fact that we’re in a dragon’s lair, could the assistant’s parent be a dragon? What an unpleasant way to be born.

However, I’ve heard from Filolial-sama and the others that the assistant’s future self was quite caring. The debt of gratitude Filolial-sama owes is a debt I owe as well. Even if she is a dragon’s child, I must repay that debt.
“Your father…”
Struggling to find the right words to persuade her, the Assistant scratches her cheek.
“Gau!”
The monster the Assistant had been hugging began to toddle away.
“Ah, wait! Don’t go! You have to wait!”
“Gau gau!”
“Eh…? But… my dad…”
“Gau!”
The monster circled around behind the Assistant and nudged her toward Father with its head.
“O-okay… so if I go with this person… is that okay?”
“Gau!”
Diving under the Assistant’s legs, the monster carried her on its back and came over to Father.
“Just for a little while… please.”
“Okay. Well then… let’s go.”
Nodding briefly, my Father glared at the adventurers, then took Keel and the Assistant by the hand and stepped out of the den.
“I’ll take care of this kid. As for the rest of you, do as you please. See you later.”
With that, my Father headed over to where we were waiting outside the den.
“Alright, everyone, let’s move on from here.”
Sakura and Luna seemed a bit reluctant with the dragon’s associates present, but they nodded in response to the Ki my Father exuded and began walking. And so, we left the dragon’s lair.
After leaving the lair and descending the mountain a short distance, Father looked at the Assistant and spoke.
“Well then… what should we do?”
Keel gently approached the assistant and told her to cheer up.
“First, may I ask you a question?”
“…Yes.”
“What’s your name?”
“…Wyndia.”
“Wyndia, huh. What do you want to do from here on out?”
“I’m going to look for my dad.”

Father was at a loss for words at the assistant’s reply. That’s right—judging by the situation, the assistant’s parent—the dragon—must be the one Ren defeated. In other words, it’s no longer in this world.
“…I have something I’d like to ask you first. Is that okay?”
“Yeah.”
“A terrible reality so painful it makes you feel like you’re going mad, or a dream you pursue with hope in your heart… which would you choose?”
Upon hearing these words, the assistant realized what he was trying to explain, lowered her head, and shed tears.
“Big bro, that’s so mean!”
“I know, but if I hadn’t pulled her out of there, she might have ended up in an even worse situation, you know? I also want to ask her what she wants to do from here on out.”
“B-but!”
“Even so, she has to decide for herself.”
“Big bro…”
“Growl.”
The monster carrying the Assistant, looking worried, tried to encourage her.
“Yeah… I’m okay. Thank you.”
After she stopped crying, the assistant looked up and told her Father.
“Please… take me to my father.”
“I see… And… I’m sorry. I couldn’t protect the things your father cherished… I could only bring you two out of there.”

The monster carrying the assistant trudged along. Given the circumstances, after all. There’s no way I could say something like, “Let’s take all the dragon’s treasure from there.” Not only would the true identity of the Divine Bird Saint be exposed, but the battle might destroy everything. Well, if it were up to me, I could’ve wiped them all out and made it all disappear, but…

“My dad told me once. He said that someday, the time might come when he dies. When that happens, he said, ‘If you have time to grieve, protect yourself instead…’ My little sister just scolded me for that.”
“That girl is…”
“Gau?”
“Yes. She’s my little sister.”
The assistant bravely smiled as she addressed her Father and Keel.
“Thank you very much.”
“No need to thank us yet. We haven’t granted your wish just yet.”
“That’s right. I’ll protect Wyndia-chan!”
“Keel, you shouldn’t be so reckless either. Stepping out in front of so many adventurers like that was incredibly dangerous, you know?”
Father scolded Keel.
“Ugh… okay, big bro. I won’t do anything reckless anymore.”
“Luna, that gave me a scare.”
“Sakura, too—”
“Luna-chan and Sakura-chan, this girl might have the scent of a dragon, but you two mustn’t fight her, okay?”
“Iwa, got it—”
“Yeah, Sakura knows that much, too.”
Filolial-sama and the others are so obedient. They’re a breath of fresh air for me, who’s been stressed out by all these unpleasant events.

“If I’d slaughtered that whole group, I could’ve had it all to myself. What? It’d be a piece of cake for me. If I wiped out all the evidence and witnesses from this world, there’d be no crime at all.”
“Huh!? Motoyasu-kun, please stop it.”

As expected, my Father stopped me. Well, I must admit I do have some hesitation about acting on behalf of my Assistant, who’s connected to the Dragon. I’m not so crude as to steal someone else’s credit. As for the Dragon’s treasure—you can easily get your hands on that just by heading deep into the mountains.
After that, my Father slowly made his way down the mountain with my Assistant and that monster. On the way back, Father checked in with the assistant once more.
“Wyndia, up ahead…”
The assistant nodded quietly and slowly gazed at the massive dragon’s carcass from the path carved into the rock face.
Trembling uncontrollably, the assistant began to shed large tears from her eyes. Father gently embraced her along with her monster.
“You don’t have to hold it in. I’ll make sure no sound escapes. You… mustn’t suppress those feelings.”
“Uuuu…”
My father pulled the Assistant close beneath his robe and let her cry her heart out. To prevent her sobs from echoing, he had Sakura-chan and the others cast wind magic to muffle the sound.
“Waaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
Leaning against my father’s chest, the Assistant cried for a long time.
